purpose: Resolve whether the observed request-context lift is likely to require explicit context-item or context-user interactions rather than an additive scorer, and identify leakage-safe architectures suitable for the fixed temporal evaluation.
query: Empirical studies of context-aware feature interactions for recommendation ranking, especially tab, time-of-day, and weekday signals in within-user impression ranking; compare additive models with explicit interaction architectures and report GAUC, nDCG@5, cold-start, and temporal generalization results.

purpose: Resolve the objective-design uncertainty after successive RankNet and hybrid-loss declines, particularly whether a top-k or listwise objective is better aligned with the severe nDCG@5 failures in low-performing tabs without changing the fixed evaluation.
query: Literature comparing RankNet, listwise ranking, LambdaRank, and top-k or nDCG-aligned objectives for implicit-feedback recommendation with logged impression groups; focus on cases where pairwise training improves or fails to improve nDCG@5 and within-user ranking metrics.
